nodes.summary: For a graph $H$ on $k$ vertices, a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices and $k \le l \le n$, the induced density of $H$ in $G$ is the average of its induced densities in the subgraphs of $G$ induced on the $l$-subsets of vertices:
nodes.title: Averaging identity for induced densities

nodes.summary: For a graph $H$ on $k$ vertices, a graph $G$ and a finite set $L$ of vertices, $p(H, G[L])$ is the proportion of the $k$-subsets of $L$ that induce a copy of $H$ in $G$: their number divided by $\binom{|L|}{k}$. It is the induced density of $H$ in the subgraph of $G$ induced on $L$.
nodes.title: Induced density of H inside a vertex set

nodes.summary: For a graph $H$ on $k$ vertices and a finite graph $G$, the induced density $p(H, G)$ is the probability that a uniformly random $k$-subset of the vertices of $G$ induces a copy of $H$. It is $0$ when $G$ has fewer than $k$ vertices. These densities, written $p(M, N)$ for finite models of a universal theory, are the basic quantities of Razborov's flag algebras; the averaging identity is their basic relation.
nodes.title: Induced density

nodes.summary: A triple $(u, v, w)$ is an ordered triangle of $G$ exactly when $u$, $v$ and $w$ are pairwise adjacent.
nodes.title: Membership in the ordered triangles

nodes.summary: The ordered triples $(u, v, w)$ of vertices of a finite simple graph $G$ that are pairwise adjacent. They are the homomorphisms from the triangle $K_3$ to $G$, so their number is six times the number of triangles, and dividing it by $n^3$ gives the homomorphism density $t(K_3, G)$ of graph-limit theory.
nodes.title: Ordered triangles of a graph

nodes.summary: For every edge density $a \in [0, 1]$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $N$ such that every simple graph on $n \ge N$ vertices with at least $a\binom{n}{2}$ edges has at least $(h(a) - \varepsilon)\binom{n}{3}$ triangles, where $h$ is Razborov's triangle density function.
nodes.title: Razborov's minimum triangle density theorem

nodes.summary: For $a \le 1/2$, Razborov's function satisfies $h(a) = 0$: complete bipartite graphs are triangle-free and realise every edge density up to $1/2$ asymptotically.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
